aula.objetivo: Choose between the pretérito indefinido and the imperfecto when telling a story: the imperfecto sets the scene, the indefinido moves the story forward, and the same verb can shift meaning (sabía × supe, conocía × conocí, quería × quise). Learn «había» and «hubo», and the difference between «salir de» and «irse».

blocos.titulo: Imperfecto for the setting, indefinido for the event
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: think of a story like a movie. First comes the setting: the time, the weather, the place, how people were. Then come the events, one after another. STEP 2: the setting goes in the imperfecto, because it's ongoing with no marked start or end: «Eran las ocho, hacía frío y yo esperaba el autobús» (it was eight, it was cold, and I was waiting for the bus). STEP 3: each event goes in the indefinido, because it starts and ends: «De repente llegó Marta y me saludó» (suddenly Marta arrived and said hello). STEP 4: ask each verb two questions. «Did this happen once and finish?» Then use the indefinido. «Was this ongoing, or how things were at that moment?» Then use the imperfecto. STEP 5: when an ongoing action gets interrupted, the ongoing one goes in the imperfecto and the one that interrupts goes in the indefinido: «Dormía cuando sonó el teléfono» (I was sleeping when the phone rang). STEP 6: a sequence of events, one after another, all stays in the indefinido: «Llegué, abrí la puerta, vi una carta y la leí» (I arrived, opened the door, saw a letter, and read it). STEP 7: the markers help. Indefinido: ayer, un día, aquel día, de repente, el lunes, una vez, a las tres. Imperfecto: siempre, cada día, todos los veranos, de niño, mientras, normalmente. STEP 8: in Spain, for a period that hasn't ended (esta mañana, hoy), the event uses the pretérito perfecto, while the setting stays in the imperfecto: «Esta mañana llovía y he llevado el paraguas». In Latin America people say «Esta mañana llovía y llevé el paraguas».
blocos.comparacao: English's simple past covers both roles here with no change in form at all — «it was raining» (ongoing) and «it rained» (a finished event) are the closest English gets, using «was/were + -ing» versus the plain past, but English speakers routinely blur that line in casual speech. Spanish forces the choice every single time, with two completely different verb forms, so this lesson's two questions — «did it happen once and finish?» versus «was it ongoing or how things were?» — aren't a check on something you already do instinctively; they're a habit to build from scratch.

exemplos.ru: Eran las diez y yo leía cuando oí un ruido.
exemplos.pt: It was ten o'clock and I was reading when I heard a noise.

exemplos.ru: Llovía mucho, así que me quedé en casa.
exemplos.pt: It was raining hard, so I stayed home.

exemplos.ru: Mientras esperaba el tren, perdí el teléfono.
exemplos.pt: While I was waiting for the train, I lost my phone.

exemplos.ru: Un día mi hermano llegó muy contento.
exemplos.pt: One day my brother arrived really happy.

tabela.exemplo: [misto] Todos los veranos íbamos al pueblo.

tabela.pergunta: [misto] Is it a description, time, age, weather?
tabela.exemplo: [misto] Eran las ocho y hacía frío.

tabela.pergunta: [misto] Was it ongoing when something happened?

erros.motivo: «Ayer» signals a single, finished event, which calls for the indefinido.

erros.errado: [misto] De niño fui al pueblo cada verano.
erros.certo: [misto] De niño iba al pueblo cada verano.
erros.motivo: A past habit calls for the imperfecto.
The ongoing action is the imperfecto; the one that interrupts is the indefinido.

erros.errado: [misto] Llovía y de repente un coche paraba.
erros.certo: [misto] Llovía y de repente un coche paró.
erros.motivo: «De repente» marks a single event: indefinido.

blocos.enunciado: Narrate out loud a short scene with a setting and an event, like «Eran las… y hacía… cuando de repente…». Use at least one verb in the imperfecto and two in the indefinido.
Conjugate «ser», «ir», and «ver» in the imperfecto, and «ir» in the indefinido. Say one sentence describing a past habit and another about a single event.
